text:
devin: Heads-up — after the slab-coalescing change I pushed last night we're seeing OOMs on a few large-chat canaries (32k tokens). Posting profiler + config so we can triage.

maria: ugh, saw the alert. are these OOMs during generation or during KV flush/compaction?

devin: during generation; memory climbs steadily after 16k and then spikes when compaction runs. stack traces show big memcpy peaks in BlockManager::compact().

sanjay: can you paste the allocator config you deployed?

devin:
```
allocator:
  slab_size: 32MB
  enable_coalesce: true
  coalesce_max_merge: 4
  reuse_hot_blocks: true
  compaction_threshold_pct: 60
  workspace_reserve_pct: 12
```

devin: note I lowered workspace reserve to 12% to try to reduce wasted headroom; maybe that made compaction more aggressive.

elaine: perf-bot posted a allocation profile earlier — devin, you ok with me pasting it? it's noisy but shows many small frees followed by a large compact pass.

devin: please paste.

perf-bot: [auto-report] allocation-sample: heap_total=14.8GB, heap_used=14.2GB, kv_cache=6.1GB, slab_free_frag=21%, memcpy_time=420ms/frame during compaction

maria: memcpy_time 420ms/frame is huge. Compaction looks like it's scanning many cold blocks. Are we merging too eagerly? coalesce_max_merge=4 might be causing big contiguous moves.

sanjay: idea: limit coalesce to same-age generations only and add a byte-range bitmap to avoid scanning cold blocks. Also add a compaction budget (ms) so we don't hit a long pause.

devin: +1 on compaction budget. also we should probe increase workspace_reserve_pct back to 20% for large contexts; the reserve avoids compaction by giving short-term slack.

elaine: quick A/B I ran: master vs revert-coalesce on canary-3 (32k ctx). revert had 0 OOMs in 24h, new had 3. revert avg latency +3% but no OOMs.

maria: we need a middle ground — keep coalescing for steady-state but avoid full compaction for burst allocations. Maybe add a reuse-hot-blocks fast-path that refuses to move blocks marked hot_by_access.

devin: implemented a prototype that short-circuits compaction for hot blocks and adds a 50ms compaction_budget. bench on canary-3 looks promising: memcpy spikes down to ~80ms/frame and no OOMs in 2h.

sanjay: can you share the prototype config snippet and the new heuristic?

devin:
```
allocator:
  enable_coalesce: true
  coalesce_policy: "same_gen_only"
  coalesce_max_merge: 2
  reuse_hot_blocks: true
  hot_block_age_threshold: 3   # touches
  compaction_budget_ms: 50
  workspace_reserve_pct: 20
```

maria: looks good. also bumping coalesce_max_merge to 2 instead of 4 reduces worst-case memmove size. hot_block_age_threshold prevents moving KV cache pages.

elaine: any risks? e.g., long-term fragmentation growth if we avoid compaction on hot blocks?

sanjay: fragmentation will increase a bit but we can trigger full compaction during low-load windows or when fragmentation > X% for > Y minutes. add metrics: slab_free_frag and compaction_runs.

devin: added metrics and an operator command `allocator.force_compact()` gated to low-load. I'll roll the prototype to canary-3 and canary-5, monitor mem growth and memcpy timings. will report back in ~6h.

maria: thanks. also open a regression ticket linking the profiler traces and canary results so PMs know impact.

devin: filed RD-3147 with attachments. tagging @eng-sre for watch. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [note] rolling canary deploy started on canary-3, canary-5. Watch allocator.slab_free_frag and memcpy_time.

elaine: nice triage everyone — keeping compaction bounded and favoring reuse seems to be the right trade-off for large contexts.

devin: agreed. follow-up: we should consider a policy that switches coalescing aggressiveness based on median seq-length per route (per-route heuristics). I'll sketch in infra RFC next week.
